what: The one comps engine's file: every reading every screen prints. One program (deliverables/20261007/comps-engine/tools/engine.mjs) wrote this file and names/<TICKER>.json; the Hub's COMPS tab, the cards, the knockout and the allocation tool read them and compute nothing of their own.
price_is: the 2026-10-06 regular-session close (chart API /quotes, captured 2026-10-07T03:57:17Z); a screen with a fresh live price divides it by the same earnings and scales the range by price ÷ close

rule.forward: price ÷ the next four quarters of consensus EPS (the dashboard's rule, lib/forward-basis.mjs); a foreign reporter's EPS in dollars at the supplier's own paired rate
rule.growth: the four quarters after the next four ÷ the next four − 1
rule.peg: that forward P/E ÷ that growth — the PEG ratio, called PEG everywhere

prior.words: growth and PEG weigh most (Alan's rule); each weight on the page is prior × coverage × fit, measured in the set, then halved where the consistency check flags the yardstick

rule.peers: the four sources vote (FMP peers, Massive related, same industry, shared fund); business lines from the filings decide membership; every line worth a tenth of the company's revenue seats its two best peers; same-business peers set the price when at least 4 exist and adjacent peers blend in at 0.35; every peer weighed by closeness (size ÷ 0.7 decade, growth ÷ 30 points, margin ÷ 20 points)
rule.outliers: expensive ones only: a multiple leaves its yardstick when it sits more than 3.5 spreads above the set's middle (log scale, median and median absolute deviation); a peer leaves every yardstick when it is that far above on 3 or more of the five (or half of those it has, at least two), or more than 2.5 spreads above on four of the five, or when taking it out alone lowers the centre by more than 10% and it is marked above. A cheap peer is never left out.
rule.growth_cap: the growth yardstick counts growth up to 30% a year, for the company and for every peer; growth beyond it is credited through the yardstick's weight, not its price
rule.not_a_target: the reading says "not a target" when more than 50% of the gap between the price and the centre comes from the growth yardstick and the centre is at least 25% above the price; or when every same-business peer that prices it is under 25% of its size and the centre is at least 50% above the price
rule.consistency: a yardstick whose implied price is more than ×1.5 from the weighted middle of the others is flagged with its reason and its weight is cut: to half at ×1.5, and by the square of the distance beyond (a tenth at ×3)
rule.debt: discount off the centre: 0% up to 2.5×, 3% up to 4×, 6% up to 6×, 10% above; + 1% per year of free cash flow beyond 5 to repay all debt (cap 5%)
